title: Rung pairs feed world px into the band_screen parameter; inline comments cite draw-path numbers the calls do not compute
evidence: Signature: "congested_halo_width :: proc(band_screen, scale: f32) -> f32 { return max(band_screen + 5.0 * scale, CONGESTION_HALO_FLOOR_WORLD * scale) }". Test comment: "Representative band values = the covenant stroke at each rung (standard tier: 3.5 world @ Core/Distribution, 4.5 @ Access; screen = world x scale per rung)" then passes {3.5, 1.4, "Distribution"} and {4.5, 2.0, "Access rest"} (world values, unconverted). Comment: "floor engages at Core fit (8.5 -> 12) and Distribution (11.9 -> 16.8)" — but congested_halo_width(3.5, 1.4) computes max(3.5+7, 16.8) = max(10.5, ...), and "expect_f32(t, congested_halo_width(4.5, 2.0), 24.0) // max(9+10, 24) at scale 2 — LITERALS" describes max(19, 24) while the call evaluates max(14.5, 24).
detail: Assertions are correct (the floor dominates at these rungs, so world-fed and draw-path inputs coincide at 16.8/24), but the pair table and comments misdescribe what is computed: 10.5 vs the cited 11.9, 14.5 vs the cited 9+10.
recommended_fix: Pass screen-converted bands ({4.9, 1.4}, {9.0, 2.0}) or relabel the comment as law-level (not draw-path) values; fix the "max(9+10, 24)" and "11.9" literals to match the actual calls.

title: Palcheck §8 routed legs index pipe_congestion unguarded; premise-broken fixture panics instead of failing clean
evidence: Legs (a)/(b)/(c) are guarded: "if testing_lvl_ok { state.crisis.pipe_congestion[ps8] = .Amber" (1424-1425, same at 1435, 1448). The (d)+(e) routed block is not: "sv_rw := view.route_wires ... view.route_wires = true ... state.crisis.pipe_congestion[ps8] = .Amber" (1466-1470). The resize that grows the slice runs only under "if testing_lvl_ok && int(ps8) >= len(state.crisis.pipe_congestion)" (1373-1374).
detail: If the fixture premise breaks (testing_lvl_ok false, no resize), line 1470 can index out of bounds — the section crashes with a traceback instead of reporting the premise check failure at 1390 and returning cleanly.
recommended_fix: Wrap the (d)+(e) routed block in the same `if testing_lvl_ok { ... }` guard as legs (a)-(c).
